paper.title: Minimal Exploration in Structured Stochastic Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Generic structured stochastic MAB (finite arms, known structure Theta, known observation family nu)
unmapped: Observation distribution nu(theta(x)) from a generic known family (not restricted to a named noise class)
Reward mu(x,theta) is deterministic and unobserved; only Y(x,t) with mean theta(x) is observed
Parameter theta lies in a known compact set Theta encoding the structure
settings.definition_quote: In each round, the decision maker selects an arm from a finite set $\cX$. Each arm $x\in\cX$ has an unknown parameter $\theta(x)\in \mathbb{R}$, and when this arm is chosen in round $t$, the decision maker observes a real-valued random variable $Y(x,t)$ with expectation $\theta(x)$ and distribution $\nu(\theta(x))$. ... The parameter $\theta$ lies in a compact set $\Theta$ that encodes the structural properties of the problem.

settings.name_in_paper: Generic structured stochastic MAB with Bernoulli observations (Assumption 2)
unmapped: Parameter theta lies in a known compact set Theta encoding the structure
Reward mu(x,theta) deterministic, known function of theta, continuous in theta
Divergence D continuous where finite (Assumption 4); unique solution of the lower-bound optimisation problem (Assumption 6)

settings.name_in_paper: Generic structured stochastic MAB with Gaussian observations (Assumption 3)
unmapped: Parameter theta lies in a known compact set Theta encoding the structure
Reward mu(x,theta) deterministic, known function of theta, continuous in theta
Divergence D continuous where finite (Assumption 4); unique solution of the lower-bound optimisation problem (Assumption 6)

symbols.C_lin: C(theta): value of the semi-infinite LP min sum_x eta(x)(mu*-mu(x,theta)) s.t. sum_x eta(x) D(theta,lambda,x) >= 1 for all confusing lambda in Lambda(theta)

source.label: th:low
source.quote: Let $\pi\in \Pi$ be a uniformly good algorithm. For any $\theta\in \Theta$, we have: \lim\inf_{T\to\infty} \frac{R^\pi(T,\theta)}{\ln~T} \ge C(\theta), where $C(\theta)$ is the value of the optimization problem ...

results.notes: Proof applies Graves & Lai (1997). Regret is defined with deterministic rewards, i.e. pseudo-regret.

symbols.C_lin: C(theta): value of the lower-bound semi-infinite LP
symbols.F_eg: F(epsilon,gamma,theta), function tending to 1 as epsilon,gamma -> 0

extra_assumptions: Assumptions 1,4,5,6: unique optimal arm, continuity of D and mu, unique solution of the optimisation problem

source.label: th:optimal
source.quote: If Assumptions~\ref{ass:unique}, \ref{as:div_continuous}, \ref{as:mu_continuous} and \ref{ass:unique_sol} hold and either Assumption~\ref{ass:bernoulli} or \ref{ass:gaussian} holds, then under the algorithm $\pi=$OSSB($\varepsilon,\gamma$) with $\varepsilon < {1 \over |\cX|}$ we have: \lim\sup_{T\to\infty} {R^\pi(T) \over \ln~T} \le C(\theta) F(\varepsilon,\gamma,\theta), with $F$ a function such that ... $F(\varepsilon,\gamma,\theta) \to 1$ as $\varepsilon\to 0$ and $\gamma \to 0$.

results.notes: Bernoulli case of Theorem 2. Proof gives F = (1+2 eps psi/C)(1+gamma). Per-round computation requires solving a semi-infinite LP; complexity not stated in general.

symbols.G_gK: G(gamma,|X|), finite constant from concentration Lemma 2
symbols.delta_k: delta(kappa) > 0, continuity radius such that C(lambda)<=C(theta)(1+kappa) etc.

source.number: Section 6 / Appendix B (finite-time bound in proof of Theorem 2)
source.quote: Putting everything together we obtain the finite-time regret upper bound: R^{\pi}(T) \le \mu^\star(\theta) \left( G(\gamma,|\cX|) +  {2 |\cX| \over \varepsilon \delta^2(\kappa)}\right) + (C(\theta)(1 + \kappa) + 2 \varepsilon \psi(\theta) ) (1+\gamma) \ln~T.

results.notes: Not in a formal theorem environment; derived in proof sketch and appendix. Holds under Bernoulli or Gaussian assumption; recorded here for Bernoulli and as r5 for Gaussian. G and delta(kappa) not explicit.

source.quote: Putting everything together we obtain the finite-time regret upper bound: R^{\pi}(T) \le \mu^\star(\theta) \left( G(\gamma,|\cX|) +  {2 |\cX| \over \varepsilon \delta^2(\kappa)}\right) + (C(\theta)(1 + \kappa) + 2 \varepsilon \psi(\theta) ) (1+\gamma) \ln~T.

results.notes: Gaussian case of the finite-time bound; same caveats as r4.
